channel.title: The Lawrence Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Lawrence Times (lawrencekstimes.com)

item.title: Tom Harper: Ben Graham’s craftsmanship preserves Lawrence buildings, compels with its details (Column)
item.description: Lawrence has benefited from Ben Graham’s generous spirit and broad skillset, particularly as a plasterer, since 1985, Tom Harper writes in this column.

item.title: Kaw Valley Almanac for March 23-29, 2026
item.description: The dust in the foreground is pollen coming off a male eastern red cedar tree last week. Expect the trees to replenish and send out enough pollen to make it miserable for allergy sufferers in coming days.

item.title: Douglas County judge sets hearing over Kansas anti-trans ‘bathroom bill’ for Sept. 29
item.description: A lawsuit challenging the constitutionality of Kansas’ new law regulating bathroom use in government buildings and forcing Kansans to hold documents reflecting their biological sex at birth won’t have its next hearing until September.

item.title: Some Lawrence residents received other people’s utility bills; here’s how to get the correct bill
item.description: The City of Lawrence believes around 5,000 customers received copies of other people’s print utility bills dated March 16. Here's how to get the correct bill, according to the city.

item.title: Lawrence Public Schools superintendent announces administrative shakeup
item.description: The Lawrence Public Schools superintendent announced new appointments and changes coming to several district positions Monday evening during the school board's meeting, including naming the principal for Centennial Choice Campus.

item.title: Lawrence community members, area activists rally and march for trans rights
item.description: Community members gathered Monday evening at South Park and marched down Massachusetts Street to protest for transgender rights amid the recent passage of anti-trans legislation.

item.title: KU chancellor defends finances, calls for unity after ‘no confidence’ vote
item.description: KU Chancellor Doug Girod defended recent budget decisions and urged unity in the KU community following an unofficial vote in which nearly 80% of respondents said they had lost confidence in the university’s leadership.

item.title: Kansas Legislature allows cities and counties to give no-bid contracts for projects up to $100K
item.description: Kansas city and county governments could award no-bid construction contracts up to $100,000 under a bill that seeks to raise the ceiling for mandatory public bidding processes.

item.title: Ben Ahlvers wants the Lawrence Arts Center to be flexible, not fragile
item.description: Ben Ahlvers is taking over the Lawrence Arts Center helm as executive director during a time of "seismic evolution." He wants to build an organization that is flexible but not fragile.

item.title: Man charged with murder in Lawrence woman’s stabbing death will face jury trial
item.description: Aaron Blake Wright will face a jury trial on a charge of second-degree murder in the stabbing death of Jina Anne Reyes-Woehler after his attorneys struggled to mount a defense implying Reyes-Woehler was a “fighter.”

item.title: Nuclear company now says Kansas reactor buried 1 mile underground might not happen
item.description: Deep Fission is clarifying priorities for the company's 1-mile underground nuclear reactor site in Kansas, now saying the group is only committed to drilling data acquisition wells in Parsons. It's unclear if a reactor will be completed.

item.title: KU researcher wins competitive NASA fellowship
item.description: Hayley Beltz, a postdoctoral researcher at KU, has earned the highly competitive NASA Hubble Prize Fellowship.
